findings.passage: "We feel like if you're going to vote for the most powerful man in the world, having proper identification is only reasonable."
findings.note: Missourinet quotes him, then a state senator and Senate floor leader, saying photo ID for voting would be proposed again in the 2016 session and that another senator would lead on it. The article also says the other caucus were pairing a proposed constitutional amendment with a companion bill.

findings.passage: "But, in my district, as I travel around Missouri, Missourians pretty much believe that, if you need a photo ID to rent a jet ski, you should probably have to have one to vote for the most powerful person in the world," he said.
findings.note: Fulton Sun quotes him, then Senate floor leader, on the photo ID constitutional amendment and enabling bill. Date is the article's publication date; he spoke 'Thursday' of that week.

findings.passage: "Voter ID was one of those things we thought was important to have an early discussion about," he explained.
findings.note: Same article. Explains why the Senate would take up the photo ID bills early in the 2016 session.
